data.name: Teressa
data.gender_notes: Teressa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Teres, meaning 'to reap' or 'harvest' in Greek. Teressa is a name of Greek origin, symbolizing the act of reaping or gathering the earth's bounty. In Christianity, Teressa is associated with the Virgin Mary, who is often depicted as the one who gathers the fruits of the earth. The name Teressa carries the meaning “Harvester of the earth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Teressa usually hope their child will grow to embody harvester of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Teressa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Harvester of the earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Teressa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Teressa has a rich cultural heritage, originating from the Greek language. In its original context, Teressa's name represents the act of reaping or harvesting, which is an essential aspect of Greek agriculture and economy. Graceful and elegant, the name Teressa has a strong cultural association with the abundance of the earth.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Teressa is a name imbued with spiritual meaning. Teressa honors the Virgin Mary, who is often invoked as the one who gathers the spiritual fruits of the Earth. Teressa embodies the idea of reaping spiritual blessings and bounties through faith, devotion, and good works. It serves as a reminder that, just as the earth produces physical fruits through the process of reaping, so too, does our spiritual cultivation yield spiritual riches.
